verdicts.title: Complexity Results on DPLL and Resolution
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: DPLL and resolution are two popular methods for solving the problem of propositional satisfiability. Rather than algorithms, they are families of algorithms, as their behavior depend on some choices they face during execution: DPLL depends on the choice of the literal to branch on; resolution depends on the choice of the pair of clauses to resolve at each step. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses the complexity of choosing optimal literals/clauses in DPLL and resolution (e.g., 'choosing the optimal literal to branch on in DPLL is Delta[log]^2-hard'), not any rank bound from quasipolynomial representations or DPLL tree diameter.

verdicts.title: Refutability as Recursive as Provability
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Godel numbering is an arithmetization of sintax which defines provability by coding a primitive recursive predicate, Pf(x,v). A multiplicity of researches and results all around this well-known recursive predicate are today widespread in many areas of logic and AI. verdicts.title: A Quasi-Polynomial Approximation for the Restricted Assignment Problem
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The Restricted Assignment Problem is a prominent special case of Scheduling on Parallel Unrelated Machines. For the strongest known linear programming relaxation, the configuration LP, we improve the non-constructive bound on its integrality gap from 1.9142 to 1.8334 and significantly simplify the proof.
